quests.title: The Ember Road
quests.summary: A burned road into Brightfall, a fractured shrine, a tower no one returns from. Something is moving behind the Veil, and the party is between it and what it wants.

phases.label: Reach the town of Brightfall

onComplete.text: Brightfall's gates open. The innkeeper, Sera Dolthwick, knows more than she says — and says just enough to make the burned road worth investigating.

phases.label: Investigate the burned road beyond Brightfall

onComplete.text: The signs are fresh: brands on the trees, ash where there should be mud, the smell of something wrong. The Ashen Veil came this way. Recently.

phases.label: Decide how to proceed — aid the village, pursue the cult, or consult the shrine

onComplete.text: A path chosen. Each one leads to the watchtower, eventually — just through different wreckage.

phases.label: Find the fracture point where the Veil has begun to bleed through

onComplete.text: The fracture is small enough to miss if you are not looking. Large enough that something has been using it for months. The old watchtower was built to watch for exactly this.

phases.label: Enter the Old Watchtower at Gloomridge

onComplete.text: The tower's interior is older than the records say. Whoever built it knew what they were keeping watch for. The thing waiting at the top has been here longer than the tower.

phases.label: Confront the Emberwood Guardian — fight, bargain, or redeem

onComplete.text: The guardian is resolved — one way or another. The route beyond is open.

phases.label: Seal the fracture or claim the watchtower beacon — open the route to Act 2

onComplete.text: The Veilscar is ahead. Whatever the Ashen Veil was preparing in the Emberwood was only the first step. The next one is longer.

quests.title: What the Veil Remembers
quests.summary: The Veilscar is not a region — it is an open wound. The Herald operates here, and the Herald has been expecting someone to come. The party's Act 1 choices shape which doors are open and which are already locked.

phases.label: Cross into the Veilscar region

onComplete.text: The Veilscar is worse than the reports. The ash is not falling — it is rising. The cult presence is visible, organized, and expecting trouble. The Herald's network has had months to prepare. The party has had the journey here.

phases.label: Map the Herald's operation — supply lines, safehouses, cell structure

onComplete.text: The Thornwhisper Circle's operative Nessa Sorroway has been building the same map for eighteen months. She shares it — or parts of it, carefully calibrated to what she has decided the party needs. The Herald is running three simultaneous operations. One of them is visible. Two are not.

phases.label: Align with a faction strategy to penetrate the Herald's inner operations

onComplete.text: The approach is set. Every faction has something useful and something they want in return. The Herald will notice eventually — the question is how much work can be done before that.

phases.label: Disrupt at least two of the Herald's three active operations

onComplete.text: Two operations are down. The third — the one involving the Plague Fen samples — is still running, and now the Herald knows the party is here. The quality of the response makes it clear: the Herald is not improvising.

phases.label: Discover the link between the Herald and the Sovereign

onComplete.text: The connection is not a chain of command. The Herald is not taking orders — the Herald is building something for the Sovereign that the Sovereign cannot build from inside the Rift. The Sovereign's Crown artifact is real, and it is almost complete.

phases.label: Confront the Ashen Veil Herald

onComplete.text: The Herald is resolved. The Crown is not complete — but the Sovereign is no longer waiting patiently. Whatever comes next will come from inside the Riftgate.

phases.label: Secure the route to the Riftgate

onComplete.text: The Riftgate is ahead. The Sovereign's influence is already bleeding past it. The party goes forward.

quests.title: The Sovereign's Terms
quests.summary: The Riftgate is not a door. It is a negotiation that has been in progress for thirty years. The Sovereign has been waiting for the party — not this party specifically, but a party sufficient to the conversation. The ending depends on what the party has become.

phases.label: Force or find a way through the Riftgate's outer defenses

onComplete.text: The outer defenses were designed to stop an army, not a party that has been moving for two acts. Inside, the architecture is wrong — built for something with different spatial assumptions than humans. The Sovereign's presence is not metaphorical. It is architectural.

phases.label: Navigate the Architect's Verge to reach the Sovereign's approach

onComplete.text: The Verge was built before the Ashen Veil. Before the Brightfall Council. Before the compact. Whatever the Architects were doing here, they were doing it with the full knowledge of what the Rift is and what it wants. There are warnings in eleven languages. The twelfth language does not have a name in any record the party has found.

phases.label: Cross Ember Hollow — the Sovereign's corrupted approach

onComplete.text: Ember Hollow was a community once. Forty-six years ago. The collapse was described as a geological event in the Brightfall Council records. The bodies in the right positions for a geological event. The buildings are not.

phases.label: Reach the Sovereign's chamber at the Rift's edge

onComplete.text: The chamber is not what was expected. The Sovereign is not a monster. It is a person — or was, or is becoming something that was a person once and retains the grammar of personhood without all of its content. It speaks. It has been speaking. It has been waiting for someone to hear it correctly.

phases.label: Confront the Emberveil Sovereign — fight, parley, or witness ascension

onComplete.text: The Sovereign is resolved. The Rift remains — but its relationship to the world has changed in some way that will take years to understand.

phases.label: Seal the Rift, collapse it, or leave it open — and get out

onComplete.text: The Riftgate is behind them. Whatever the Ember Rift becomes from here is something the world will have to live with. The party has done what parties do: they made it through. What follows is not a party problem. It is an era problem.

quests.title: The Tracking Log
quests.summary: Lyra has been following the cult cell that killed her mother for two years. She has a name, a location, and a problem: she cannot act alone without destroying the evidence trail. She needs help she does not know how to ask for.

phases.label: Lyra shares her tracking log

onComplete.text: She produces a folded journal from her pack. Two years of notation: dates, locations, cult cell activity, one name circled in red. 'I found where he operates. I cannot go there alone without tipping them. I have been waiting for a reason to trust someone.' She closes the journal. 'This is me trusting.'

phases.label: Find the hidden scout post Lyra marked on her map

onComplete.text: The cache is exactly where she said it would be: hollow oak at the fen-edge, sealed watertight. Inside: a ledger of cult supply routes in handwriting she recognizes as her mother's. Her mother was tracking them before Lyra was.

phases.label: Confront the cult operator Lyra has been tracking

onComplete.text: It ends badly for the cult operator and incompletely for Lyra — the information matters more than the closure, and she knows it, and that is the part that costs something.

phases.label: Help Lyra decide what to do with her mother's ledger

onComplete.text: She gives the ledger to the guild. 'She built it for this. I am not going to stop carrying it.' She does not say thank you. She does not need to.

quests.title: The Resignation Letter
quests.summary: Captain Maer resigned rather than burn a village. She still has the letter she was ordered to deliver. She never delivered it. She is not sure what to do about that — or the village, which is still standing, and still exposed.

phases.label: Maer describes the order she refused

onComplete.text: 'The order cited cult-sympathizer grounds. The assessment was mine. I wrote it three months earlier about general Ashen Veil activity in the area — not about that village specifically. Someone used it anyway.' She does not use the word 'falsified.' She uses 'repurposed.' The distinction is exact.

phases.label: Locate the village and assess its current situation

onComplete.text: Fenwold is intact. Forty-three people. A watermill. A blacksmith who sharpens the shrine-keeper's tools at no charge. The Emberguard has not followed through — whether from resource shortage or because they assumed Maer complied, they cannot know. The village does not know about the order.

phases.label: Decide whether to warn the village and how

onComplete.text: A decision with weight. The village is still here. Whatever comes next, Maer made a different choice — and so did the party.

phases.label: Maer decides what to do about the letter and the chain of command that generated it

onComplete.text: She burns the letter. 'The letter was never the problem.' She keeps the assessment. 'The assessment is accurate. Someone needs to read it correctly.'

quests.title: Where Adric Died
quests.summary: Orren has seventeen vows. One is to find where his brother died and bury him properly. He does not know yet that the patrol 'accident' was not an accident. The party may learn this before he does.

phases.label: Orren explains why he joined the march toward Gloomridge

onComplete.text: He says it quietly, the way he says most things: 'My brother Adric was on the Veilscar patrol. He died in Gloomridge. The report says 'terrain accident.' I have read the report seventeen times. There are four words that do not belong.' He does not ask you to help. He is already walking.

phases.label: Help Orren find the battle markers his brother's unit left

onComplete.text: The unit's markers are intact — Orren taught Adric the protocol himself. The markers tell a different story than the report: the patrol was not traveling toward a terrain obstacle. It was retreating from an engagement the report doesn't mention. Someone erased the engagement from the record.

phases.label: Find the full truth of what happened to Adric's patrol

onComplete.text: The patrol was deliberately routed into a cult ambush by someone in the Emberguard command chain. The order came from above Captain Maer, after Maer had already filed objections. Orren buries his brother's effects at the marker. He does not speak for a long time. When he does, his voice is exactly the same as it always is.

phases.label: Orren decides what to do with what he knows

onComplete.text: He breaks one of his seventeen vows — the one about not taking action outside sanctioned orders. He decides the sanction is now himself. 'I will not stop,' he says. It is not a threat. It is just information.

quests.title: What the Road Took
quests.summary: A caravan went quiet three days ago on the Old Road. A survivor reached Brightfall before collapsing. The Wanderers Guild wants to know what happened. So do the bandits who made it happen.

phases.label: Find the caravan survivor at the Brightfall inn

onComplete.text: The survivor, a junior guild courier named Temm, is coherent enough to describe the attack. Twisted Hand bandits, eight or more, stopped the caravan at the bridge ford. The cargo — sealed guild packets — was taken rather than destroyed. That detail is the one that matters.

phases.label: Follow the trail from the ford to the bandit camp

onComplete.text: The trail is not well hidden. The Twisted Hand did not expect to be followed — or did not care. The camp is in a collapsed mill two hours east of the ford. Eight people, the guild packets, and something else that should not be there: an Ashen Veil brand burned into the mill's main post.

phases.label: Confront the Twisted Hand — rescue, ransom, or eliminate

onComplete.text: The guild packets are recovered. The Ashen Veil connection to the Twisted Hand is a lead worth keeping.

quests.title: The Keeper's Circuit
quests.summary: Keeper Orvain tends his three shrines on foot, alone, without pay. One has been defiled. He will not ask for help — but he will accept it.

phases.label: Locate the defiled shrine in the Emberwood

onComplete.text: The shrine is older than the road it stands beside. The Ashen Veil's work is recognizable: ash circles, deliberate erasure of the ember-marks, a smell of something chemically wrong. Orvain is already here, cataloguing the damage with the practiced calm of someone who has learned not to be surprised by this.

phases.label: Gather three ember-offerings from the surrounding region

onComplete.text: Each offering required something from the land: a cinder from the old forge, fresh water from the fen-spring, a carved stone from the Stoneward ridge. Orvain receives them without ceremony. He says the shrine will decide what they mean.

phases.label: Perform the cleansing ritual — and decide what to do with what it reveals

onComplete.text: The shrine is resolved. What it showed during the ritual is not something Orvain will discuss. But he writes something in his maintenance log and signs it twice.

quests.title: The Assessment
quests.summary: Bram's patrol assessment was repurposed to justify the Veilscar incident. He has known for years. He has been building a counter-assessment that corrects the record. He needs witnesses and a way to file it that will not be intercepted.

phases.label: Bram explains the assessment and what was done with it

onComplete.text: 'I want to be precise about this.' He takes off his spectacles and cleans the enchanted lens. 'My assessment correctly described Veil activity in the patrol region. It did not recommend the patrol route, the timing, or the staffing decisions that led to the incident. Someone added three pages. I know who, approximately. I have been building a counter-assessment that would make the addition visible.' He puts the spectacles back on.

phases.label: Help Bram gather the evidence chain for his counter-assessment

onComplete.text: The evidence is assembled. The three added pages were written in a hand that almost matches Bram's — close enough to survive casual inspection. The spectacles identified the Veil-energy residue on the additions: the forger spent time near an active Rift breach before writing them. That is a very short list of people.

phases.label: Find a channel to file the counter-assessment that will not be intercepted

onComplete.text: Filed through the Thornwhisper Circle's legal access to the Iron Covenant's archive — which no one who would want to intercept it knows exists. Bram watches it go and is quiet for a moment. 'It will not fix what happened to the patrol. I have been very clear with myself about that.' He continues to be clear with himself about it for the rest of the act.

phases.label: Help Bram decide what to do with the eight seconds of Rift exposure

onComplete.text: He calibrates the enchanted lens to share what it sees. 'I have seventeen shelves of notes from eight seconds. You should have access to what I can see.' He begins writing shelf eighteen.

phases.label: Bram recuses himself if Rift data is used for exploitation

onComplete.text: 'I will not be party to the use of Veil data for commercial exploitation. I am sufficiently precise about my position to know this is the line.' He is not angry. He is precise.

quests.title: Professional Separateness
quests.summary: Tessaly's past employer was Ashen Veil. She did not know. She has spent two years ensuring she knows everything she can about the work she did on their behalf. Some of it she can undo. Some she cannot.

phases.label: Tessaly discloses her past employer in confidence

onComplete.text: She does it without preamble. 'I worked for them for eight months. Four contracts. I did not ask enough questions. I ask all the questions now.' She unrolls a detailed map of her own past work: dates, locations, outcomes. 'I need to know which of these can be undone.'

phases.label: Help Tessaly audit the outcomes of her four past contracts

onComplete.text: Three contracts were intelligence-gathering that harmed no one directly but enabled later harm. One contract resulted in a death that would not have happened without her work. She already knew. She wanted to say it to someone who knew what she meant by it.

phases.label: Help Tessaly do what can be done about the undoable contracts

onComplete.text: She routes the remediated information to the Circle through Nessa Sorroway. 'This doesn't fix it,' she says. She means the death. 'It doesn't not fix it either.' She means the rest.

phases.label: Tessaly decides what professional separateness means going forward

onComplete.text: She keeps the face-wrap on. 'It is still useful.' She takes off the habit of not asking who is hiring. 'That one cost too much.' She stays.

phases.label: Tessaly parts ways if the party sides with the Veil

onComplete.text: 'I have made this mistake before. I recognize the shape of it.' She leaves without anger. She says it is not personal. She means it.

quests.title: The Seventeenth Stone
quests.summary: Yasha's order maintained Pact-stone seventeen until it was stolen. She has been preparing for seventeen years. She has found where the stone is — it is in the Herald's possession, being used as part of the Crown construction. Getting it back means going through the Herald's sanctum.

phases.label: Yasha confirms the stone is in the Herald's sanctum

onComplete.text: She does not ask. She states: 'The seventeenth stone is in the Herald's sanctum. I have been preparing for this for seventeen years. I am ready. If the path presents itself, I will take it.' She continues healing companions and stopping at every shrine. The preparing and the waiting look exactly the same on her.

phases.label: Locate the Herald's sanctum and find a way inside

onComplete.text: The sanctum is the third operation — the one the Herald did not try to stop the party from disrupting. Yasha notes this. 'They wanted us to find it. Or they wanted someone to. The stone is not a passive object in Ashen Veil hands.'

phases.label: Enter the sanctum and recover the Pact-stone

onComplete.text: The stone resists. Not the Herald — the stone itself. It has been in Veil-saturated conditions for seventeen years. Yasha names it in the old compact language, quietly, seventeen times. The stone responds. She wraps it in her hands the way she wraps her vows each morning. 'It remembers,' she says.

phases.label: Help Yasha reconsecrate the stone at an active Pact-shrine

onComplete.text: The reconsecration takes the whole night. Yasha does not sleep. When it is done, she sits beside the shrine and is quiet. Then: 'Seventeen years.' Not a complaint. A number. A measurement of something she does not name.

phases.label: Yasha departs if the stone is destroyed

onComplete.text: 'I have vows I cannot keep in the company of those who destroy what the compact protects.' She says it plainly, without accusation. She has already gone when she finishes saying it.

quests.title: What Was Indexed
quests.summary: The Library Ruins hold an archive of pre-Sovereign research — forty years of Veil-observation records that the Brightfall Council officially does not acknowledge exist. Getting inside requires the Thornwhisper Circle's access codes. Deciding what to do with the contents is harder.

phases.label: Gain access to the Library Ruins via the Thornwhisper Circle

onComplete.text: Nessa Sorroway provides the access codes without explanation. The library's interior is intact — someone maintained it. Forty years of systematic observation, charted and cross-indexed. The Veil has been expanding for sixty years, not thirty. The official record begins at the founding of the Brightfall Council.

phases.label: Decode the archive's encrypted final section

onComplete.text: The encrypted section contains names. Council members, Emberguard commanders, Ashen Veil operatives — a documented decade of coordination. The council did not simply fail to stop the Veil's expansion. It contracted to manage the expansion's rate and direction. This is the document that changes everything, if it reaches people who can act on it.

phases.label: Decide what to do with the archive

onComplete.text: The archive's fate is decided. What follows from that decision will depend on who reads it, when, and what they choose to do.

quests.title: The Formula and the Cost
quests.summary: A bone-reader named Mira Ashbone has reverse-engineered a partial cure for the Plague Fen sickness. She needs three ingredients the Harvesters control. The Harvesters know what the cure means for their business. The side effects of the cure are real, documented, and uncomfortable.

phases.label: Find Mira Ashbone in the Ash Plains

onComplete.text: Mira has the formula. She has been testing it on herself for fourteen months to document the side effects, which she lists in the same tone she uses for everything else. The cure works. The side effects include temporary sensitivity to Veil-energy, meaning cured individuals can perceive cult activity for approximately three weeks before the sensitivity fades. This is a logistical problem for several parties.

phases.label: Acquire the three ingredients from Plague Harvester territory

onComplete.text: The Harvesters contested two of the three acquisitions. The third they did not contest, which Mira notes is suspicious — they let you have the fen-spore catalyst. She has a theory about why. She writes it down and signs it.

phases.label: Decide how and where to distribute the cure

onComplete.text: The cure is distributed — or not. Three weeks of Veil-sensitivity for the recipients, if it went out. Mira notes the final tally with the same tone she uses for everything. 'It was worth the side effects,' she says. She does not ask if the party agrees.

quests.title: The Twelfth Language
quests.summary: Bram's spectacles can read the twelfth language. Barely. It is a Rift-native notation system that predates human contact with the Ember Rift by centuries. There are forty-three glyphs in the Architect's Verge. Reading them all produces something that might be instructions, a warning, or a map of what was supposed to happen.

phases.label: Document all 43 glyphs in the Architect's Verge

onComplete.text: Forty-three glyphs. Bram's notes fill two journals. The language is not a human adaptation of something alien — it is the original, partially translated by someone who knew both systems. 'Someone was translating in both directions,' Bram says. 'This was a correspondence.'

phases.label: Complete Bram's translation of the glyph sequence

onComplete.text: The translation is not instructions or a warning. It is a record of the original negotiation: the first time a human entered the Rift willingly and came back, sixty years before the Brightfall Council's founding. The negotiator's name is in the first glyph. It is also on a portrait in the Brightfall Council chamber.

phases.label: Apply the glyph knowledge to the final confrontation

onComplete.text: The glyph knowledge changes the final confrontation — specifically, it changes what the party can say and what the Sovereign understands them to mean. The original negotiation ended badly. This one does not have to.

quests.title: The Organized Thing
quests.summary: The Oathless have coalesced at the Crossroads, eighteen former Emberguard soldiers with no charter and one shared purpose. They want to hold the Sovereigns Approach so the party can reach the Riftgate without fighting through two layers of opposition. They are asking for a plan and someone to coordinate it.

phases.label: Locate the Oathless position at the Crossroads approach

onComplete.text: Eighteen soldiers in no particular formation, well-armed, with a shared willingness to do the thing they were discharged for almost doing. Their plan has three phases and one contingency. The contingency is: if the party does not return in three days, they fall back to the Crossroads and wait for someone else.

phases.label: Coordinate the Oathless defensive position at Sovereign's Approach

onComplete.text: The position holds. The Oathless fight the same way they always did — by the training that was good, and by the judgment that got them discharged. The Ashen Veil finds the approach unexpectedly contested.

phases.label: Return to the Oathless after the final confrontation

onComplete.text: They are still there. Fourteen of eighteen, which is better than the contingency predicted. They do not ask what happened inside. They can tell from how the party looks coming back. 'Did it work?' Yes or no, they say. Then they get up and start the march back to the Crossroads.
